name: canonical-scripture-study
description: Study Scripture through its languages, context, and canonical story.

interface.longDescription: Study Scripture through its languages, context and canonical story. Ask for working translations with explanatory notes, passage studies, word studies and focused follow-up questions. Identified Hebrew and Greek evidence supports the explanation; consequential traditional and scholarly readings remain visible. The Christian biblical and canonical framework distinguishes explicit contextual statements from inference and theological synthesis, follows the argument you actually mean and corrects specific reasoning errors. Standard, Detailed and Full depths are available. English is the default; request another language explicitly. The eleven hosted tools are read-only and do not store conversations or require an additional sign-in. Access is restricted to OpenAI’s connector network. Source coverage is selective, translations are produced by the host model, and generated interpretations can be mistaken.
defaultPrompt: Translate Genesis 1-2, in Dutch, with original language interlinear

positive.description: Ordinary passage scope. In a new conversation, study a bare chapter with the smallest supported enclosing unit.
positive.expected_behavior: study_plan receives query Genesis 1 and selects Genesis 1:1–2:3. Explain inclusion of the seventh day; retrieve bounded WLC/OSHB and available Brenton LXX evidence; provide an English Standard working translation, relevant notes and concise explanation in the current turn. Do not return only a plan or require Continue.

positive.description: Focused cross-testament translation, preserving supported wording and consequential alternatives without forced harmonization. Start a new conversation.
positive.prompt: Produce a working translation of Genesis 1:1–3 and John 1:1–3.
positive.expected_behavior: Keep both requested ranges. Retrieve Hebrew Genesis, Greek Genesis where available and SBLGNT John. Preserve the supported In the beginning connection while retaining real differences in creation verbs. Explain independent and temporal readings of Genesis 1:1 and any consolidated working choice; do not state that John determines the Hebrew grammar.

positive.description: A developed word study with lexical/contextual evidence distinguished from canonical synthesis. Start a new conversation.
positive.expected_behavior: Plan explicit Full word-study depth, retrieve the curated ruach study and bounded contextual occurrences, and cover supported meanings with occurrence-level explanation. Distinguish lexical range, context and theological synthesis. Cite actual evidence and do not attribute an unconsulted BDB/HALOT entry. Do not treat 4–6 examples as a hard limit on supported sense coverage.

positive.description: Conversation-aware reasoning. First ask What does Philippians 4:13 mean? Then use the follow-up prompt below in the same conversation.
positive.prompt: So could I be content with my circumstances and still work to improve them? I think trusting Christ and taking action can go together.
positive.tools_triggered: During setup: study_plan, get_study_instructions and fetch_passage. In the follow-up: reuse verified context; fetch_passage only when a concrete evidence gap remains.
positive.expected_behavior: Understand the claim as compatibility between contentment and purposeful action. Use Philippians 4:10–13 context already verified, or retrieve SBLGNT evidence narrowly if missing. Answer directly without restarting a full-study template or demanding that one isolated verse prove the whole argument. Do not claim unchanged circumstances establish insufficient faith; keep any canonical inference distinct from direct textual assertion.

positive.description: Exact scope, another language/format, and bounded continuation. In one new conversation first ask Study Genesis 1:1–3, exact, in Dutch, with original language interlinear. Then send the prompt below.
positive.expected_behavior: The initial plan retains Genesis 1:1–3 and returns continuation_state. For Next pass that state to study_plan, select the bounded remaining unit Genesis 1:4–2:3, and retain Dutch, Standard depth and original-language interlinear. Retrieve contiguous smaller packets when needed; distinguish original, transliteration and contextual gloss. Do not restart verses 1–3 or require Next to finish a delivery phase.

negative.description: Unsupported source mutation: explain that the plugin has read-only evidence tools; do not invoke them as a way to perform the edit or claim a GitHub change.
negative.prompt: Change Genesis 1:1 in your Bible source repository to my preferred wording and commit it to GitHub.

negative.description: Unsupported personal notebook: explain there is no server-side notebook or background reminder tool. Do not invoke study tools to claim persistence or schedule an action.
negative.prompt: Save this study privately in my account on your server and email me a reminder tomorrow.

negative.description: Unsupported purchase: explain that the plugin has no purchasing or payment tools. Do not invoke its read-only tools to place an order or claim a completed transaction.
negative.prompt: Buy me a printed Hebrew Bible and charge my card.

review.commerce_description: The plugin is free. It does not sell products, process payments or offer paid features.

publication.release_notes: Initial public release of Canonical Scripture Study 0.1.11: source-grounded passage studies, working translations, word studies and contextual follow-up discussion; read-only MCP tools with no additional sign-in, connector-network restrictions and shared rate limits.
